incumbent.name: Stephen Bartels
incumbent.summary: Stephen Bartels of Eckerty, an Army veteran and Patoka Lake business owner, was chosen by a Republican caucus in November 2017 to fill the rest of Lloyd Arnold's term and has held House District 74 since {dch_2017}. He chairs the House Veterans Affairs and Public Safety Committee {caucus_bartels}.
record: Committees: Veterans Affairs and Public Safety (chair), Courts and Criminal Code, and Public Policy; co-chair of the legislature's defense caucus (2025) {caucus_bartels}. In May 2026 Gov. Mike Braun picked him to chair the Indiana Defense Task Force {caucus_taskforce}.
2023: Sponsored HEA 1017, creating a prescription drug donation repository for uninsured or underinsured low-income Hoosiers {caucus_hea1017}.

2026: Authored HEA 1003, which sunsets or restructures more than 40 state boards and commissions {caucus_hea1003}; authored HEA 1210, raising the property tax deduction for totally disabled veterans to 100% of their home's assessed value and adding other veteran credits {caucus_hea1210}; sponsored SEA 227, making the Indiana State Police the lead agency for countering drones once federal authorization exists {caucus_sea227}.

Voted yes on the 2025 budget conference report, HEA 1001 (April 25, 2025) {rc_hb1001_576}; was excused and did not vote on SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law, on April 10, 2025 {rc_sea1_433}. Was one of the Republicans who voted no on HB 1032, the congressional redistricting bill, which passed the House 57-41 on Dec. 5, 2025 {rc_hb1032_28}.

race_context: House District 74 covers all of Perry, Crawford and Spencer counties and parts of Dubois and Orange counties, per the House Republican caucus {caucus_bartels}.
Bartels won 68.6% of the vote in 2024 {wiki_2026}. He was unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary, and no Democrat appears in the primary results {wiki_2026}.
The Dubois County Free Press lists Stephen R. Bartels (R) and Lena Goffinet (D) on the Nov. 3 ballot {dcfp_ballot}.
Key differences: Goffinet has published no policy positions that we could find; her campaign website shows only a placeholder page {goffinet_site}.
No debate or forum for this race was found.

candidates.summary: Lena Goffinet is the Democratic nominee; we found almost no published information about her background or positions {ivg_goffinet}{goffinet_site}.
background: Her iVoterGuide profile lists no education, work or affiliation information {ivg_goffinet}.
path_to_ballot: Was not on the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary ballot; no Democratic primary for this seat is listed {wiki_2026}. How she was nominated was not found.
on_incumbent: No statements about Bartels or the seat's record were found.
endorsements_finance: iVoterGuide lists an endorsement from the Spencer County Democrats {ivg_goffinet}.
gaps: Campaign website (hoosiersfirst.com) showed only a "Coming Soon" page when checked; Facebook and Instagram pages were not readable.
No news coverage was found in Perry, Spencer or Dubois county outlets reviewed.
How she reached the ballot (likely a Democratic ballot-vacancy caucus after the primary) is unconfirmed.

Unverified: a May 2025 Change.org petition seeking a traffic light at the Highway 37/237 intersection in Tell City was started by a Lena Goffinet; a 2022 state licensing-board agenda lists a Lena Goffinet as a licensed social worker. Neither was confirmed to be the candidate.

candidates.summary: Stephen Bartels has held the seat since November 2017 and chairs the House Veterans Affairs and Public Safety Committee {dch_2017}{caucus_bartels}. He was unopposed in the May primary {wiki_2026}.
background: Served 22 years in the military, retiring as a major, and nine years as an Indiana law enforcement officer {caucus_bartels}.
Owns and operates Patoka Lake Marina and is owner and vintner of Patoka Lake Winery {caucus_bartels}.
Former Crawford County Council president and former president of the Crawford County Tourism Board {caucus_bartels}{dch_2017}. Lives in Eckerty {caucus_bartels}.
path_to_ballot: Was unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary {wiki_2026}.

items: Authored HEA 1210 (2026) expanding property tax relief for disabled veterans, saying it protects "their homes as a thank you for protecting ours" {caucus_hea1210}.
Authored HEA 1003 (2026) to consolidate state boards and commissions, saying it "strengthens and modernizes" how they are structured {caucus_hea1003}.
Sponsored SEA 227 (2026) on counter-drone authority, saying it "gives law enforcement the tools they need to stay ahead of emerging threats" {caucus_sea227}.
Says defense-industry growth in southern Indiana is creating high-wage careers {caucus_taskforce}.
Voted no on the December 2025 congressional redistricting bill, HB 1032 {rc_hb1032_28}.

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No statements about his challenger were found.
plans: As chair of the Indiana Defense Task Force, his 2026 bill directs state defense funding to match the task force's priorities {caucus_taskforce}.
gaps: No public statement explaining his no vote on HB 1032 was found.
No endorsements or fundraising totals were found.
